--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.current_flow_betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Calculate current-flow (random-walk) betweenness for all nodes. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.current_flow_betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Calculate current-flow (random-walk) betweenness for all nodes. title: >- [Graph.current_flow_betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Calculate current-flow (random-walk) betweenness for all nodes. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate current-flow (random-walk) betweenness for all nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L53682-L53819){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.current_flow_betweenness_centrality( normalized=True, weighted=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Current-flow betweenness centrality](../assets/graphs/current-flow-betweenness-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by current-flow betweenness, the share of electrical current through each node when every pair in turn injects and draws a unit of current. The bridge E carries the most at 0.58, then the hub C 0.43 and the tail node F 0.33; the pendant G carries none." width="100%"} Ordinary betweenness assumes everything travels along shortest paths. Current-flow betweenness (Newman 2005; Brandes & Fleischer 2005) instead treats the graph as an electrical network: for every pair of nodes, one unit of current enters at one and leaves at the other, spreading over *all* paths in proportion to their conductance, and a node's score is the total current passing through it. Equivalently, it counts how often a random walk between the pair passes through the node. This captures influence in networks where flow is not optimally routed (rumors, disease, power grids), and gives credit to nodes on near-shortest alternative routes, which shortest-path betweenness ignores. Edge weights act as conductances: heavier edges carry more current. The graph must be undirected and connected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), divide by `(n - 1)(n - 2) / 2`, the number of pairs not involving the node, so scores lie in `[0, 1]`. Matches NetworkX. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights as conductances. If `None` (default), follows the graph (weights on `Graph(weighted=True)`). Weights must be positive. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"current_flow_betweenness_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or disconnected, or a weight is not positive. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~betweenness_centrality`) : Count shortest paths only. [](`~approximate_current_flow_betweenness_centrality`) : A faster estimate for large graphs. [](`~edge_current_flow_betweenness_centrality`) : The same measure for edges. [](`~current_flow_betweenness_centrality_subset`) : Count chosen pairs only. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a square with one diagonal, shortest-path betweenness gives the corners off the diagonal no credit, because the diagonal is always shortest. Current flow still sends some of the traffic around through them: ::: {#47f0716c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec square = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A"), ("A", "C")] ) ( square.current_flow_betweenness_centrality() .betweenness_centrality() .get_node_df() .select( "label", "current_flow_betweenness_centrality", "betweenness_centrality", ) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Alternative routes In Zachary's karate club, member 3 is fifteenth by betweenness but eighth by current flow: its six friends sit in the instructor's tight circle, which offers many routes that are nearly as short as the shortest. Member 19, whose three friends include both leaders, goes the other way, from ninth to fifteenth: with so few ties, it carries little of the current on the longer routes: ::: {#4db4a1cf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl club = ( ec.karate_club() .layout_kamada_kawai() .current_flow_betweenness_centrality() .betweenness_centrality() ) ( club.get_node_df() .with_columns( pl.col("current_flow_betweenness_centrality", "betweenness_centrality") .rank("min", descending=True) .name.suffix("_rank") ) .filter(pl.col("label").is_in(["0", "33", "3", "19"])) .select( "label", "current_flow_betweenness_centrality_rank", "betweenness_centrality_rank", ) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Edge weights act as conductances, so heavier edges carry more current. A weight that measures a cost or a distance, such as the travel times in `metro()`, has the opposite meaning; pass `weighted=False` for such graphs. For large graphs, `approximate_current_flow_betweenness_centrality()` estimates the scores from a sample.
